title: Cron Job Privilege Escalation / Persistence
description: A scheduled cron job runs as a privileged user but references a script or binary that is writable by a lower-privileged user, uses a weak PATH, or operates on attacker-writable files. A local user can modify the referenced target so that their code executes with the privileges of the cron owner, enabling escalation or persistence.
businessImpact: High --- writable or insecurely configured cron jobs allow a standard user to execute code as root and to maintain persistent access.
remediation:
- Ensure scripts and binaries invoked by privileged cron jobs are owned by root and not writable by others.
- Use absolute paths and set an explicit, safe PATH in cron jobs.
- Restrict permissions on cron directories and crontab files.
- Monitor cron configuration for unauthorized changes.
